questions.question: Is the subject-name resolution (`profileMap[payload.pubkey]`) a real lookup against the live profile map with a genuine truncated-npub fallback, rather than a stub always returning a fixed display name or always hitting the fallback branch regardless of whether a profile exists? Is the author resolution genuinely wired to `senderPubkey` (mirroring `resolveCancellerDisplay`) rather than a copy-pasted call that actually still reads `payload.pubkey` under a renamed variable?

Is the `invite_lifecycle` render branch added to `renderStructuredMessage` in `ChatBox.tsx` near the `leave_intent`/`member_admitted` branches (per architecture.md's Module Map), with the presentational component `InviteLifecycleChatAnnouncement.tsx` modelled on `LeaveChatAnnouncement.tsx` kept separate from the branch-selection logic? Are the 3 new i18n keys added only to `i18n.ts` (per the project's translation convention: no hardcoded user-visible strings in components), with matching non-empty `en`/`de` entries?

Could `render` (`ChatBox.tsx`'s invite_lifecycle branch + `InviteLifecycleChatAnnouncement.tsx`) be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist (e.g. does it reach into `parse` for the type shape, or into `invite-producer`/`accept-producer` for payload construction), and do they flow through the declared `InviteLifecycleContent` seam contract rather than a redeclared local shape?

Does `app/tests/unit/chat/ChatBox.test.tsx` cover AC-RENDER-1/2/3 with tests that distinguish: (a) a known-profile subject (asserts nickname, not npub), (b) an unknown-profile subject (asserts truncated npub fallback, not a blank/undefined render), (c) all three `event` values individually with distinct copy strings asserted (not just 'a string was rendered'), and (d) a snapshot or DOM query proving the absence of avatar/bubble/edit/delete/reaction affordances (an assertion that would fail if a generic message-row wrapper were reused unmodified)?

Does the landed render branch jointly exercise AC-STRUCT-5 (S1's parse/attribution-boundary guarantee) end-to-end — i.e. is there a test in this story's suite constructing a message whose payload `pubkey` names B but whose transport `senderPubkey` is C, asserting the rendered author is C, not B? Per S1's notes, this is the render-time observable consequence S1 and S4 jointly exercise; confirm S4's test suite is where this end-to-end case actually lives (not silently dropped because each story assumed the other owned it).

Does the render branch defensively handle a `profileMap` lookup miss (undefined) without throwing — falling back to truncated npub as specified — and does it defensively handle an unrecognized `event` value reaching the render branch (should be impossible given S1's guard, but is there a safe default/no-crash path rather than an unguarded object-index into the copy-string map that could return `undefined` and render blank/literal-undefined text)?

Does rendering an `invite_lifecycle` message display the invitee (subject) name resolved from `profileMap[payload.pubkey]`'s nickname, falling back to a truncated npub when no profile is known? Provide (a) the resolution code (mirroring the `member_admitted` name-resolution precedent cited in the AC), (b) a test with a populated `profileMap` entry asserting the nickname renders, and a second test with no matching entry asserting a truncated-npub format (not raw hex, not blank), and (c) confirmation the truncation format matches the existing `member_admitted`/`LeaveChatAnnouncement` convention rather than a newly invented format.

Does rendering an `invite_lifecycle` message select its copy string from `i18n.ts` keyed on `event`, with a distinct, non-empty string present for each of `invited`/`accepted`/`declined` in both `en` and `de`? Provide (a) the new `Copy` type keys and both locale objects' entries, (b) a test rendering each of the three `event` values and asserting the exact expected copy string (not just 'copy is non-empty'), for both locales via the language context, and (c) confirmation the three strings are genuinely distinct from each other (a copy-paste that gives all three the same string would be a silent AC violation this test must catch).

Does the `invite_lifecycle` presentational component render with a stable `data-testid`, no avatar, no message bubble, and no edit/delete/reaction affordances, consistent with the `LeaveChatAnnouncement` precedent? Provide (a) the component's JSX showing the absence of these elements by construction (not merely CSS-hidden), (b) a test querying the DOM for the stable `data-testid` and asserting the absence of avatar/bubble/action-button elements, and (c) confirmation the `data-testid` value is stable across renders (not derived from a changing timestamp or random id) so downstream e2e selectors (S10) remain valid.

`selectInviteLifecycleCopy`'s `default` branch (app/src/components/groups/InviteLifecycleChatAnnouncement.tsx) silently returns `memberDisplay` for any `event` value outside the 3-member enum, with no warning/log. Since this path is only reachable if S1's parse-side enum guard were ever weakened or bypassed, is silent fallback (vs. a dev-only console.warn) the right tradeoff, or would a future regression in the parse guard now render a subtly-wrong row (missing verb, e.g. just "Alice") with no signal that the enum contract was violated?

The dev implementer's own return notes flagged that the ChatBox.tsx branch comment was reworded from a draft using the literal word "senderPubkey" to "the message's protocol-level sender", specifically to avoid tripping the new test's `not.toMatch(/senderPubkey/)` structural assertion on the extracted branch text. Does that renamed phrasing still clearly convey the AC-STRUCT-5 boundary to a future maintainer skimming the branch (i.e., is the safety property still legible without the literal token), or does optimizing the prose to satisfy a regex assertion risk quietly degrading the comment's usefulness over time as the branch is edited?

The structural source-scan test extracts the ChatBox.tsx `invite_lifecycle` branch via the regex `/if \(structured\?\.type === 'invite_lifecycle'[\s\S]*?\n    \}\n/` (app/tests/unit/chat/inviteLifecycleAnnouncement.test.ts). Is this extraction robust to an unrelated future edit elsewhere in ChatBox.tsx (e.g. reindentation, or another branch's closing brace at the same 4-space indent appearing before this branch's own closing brace), or could the regex silently match the wrong span and pass/fail for the wrong reason? Worth a maintainer note if this regex is ever seen failing after an unrelated ChatBox.tsx change.
